title: Narrate in a human-sounding conversational voice
statement: Narrate in a conversational second-person voice that sounds human, not robotic and not in a formal textbook register.
example: Personalised narration improved retention by d = 0.30 and transfer by d = 0.54, and human voices beat robotic ones at a median d = 0.74.
detail: The grade-7 science visual design guide asks for conversational, direct-address narration in a human-sounding voice, because direct address and a human voice create useful social cues (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-visuals-human-v0.1.md`, lines 180-185). It cites personalisation at d=0.30 for retention and d=0.54 for transfer (Ginns, Martin & Marsh 2013) and a human voice beating a robotic one at a median d=0.74 (Mayer, Fiorella & Stull 2020). It lists monotone robotic narration in a formal textbook register as an anti-pattern and asks for expressive, human-like synthetic speech with checked science pronunciation (lines 294 and 322), and the course's generation spec fixes one calm, natural voice per video speaking in the second person (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-generation-agent-v0.2.md`, line 41).
against: The speaking-rate band paired with this rule is an operating heuristic, not a proven threshold (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/video-visuals-human-v0.1.md`, lines 187-188). Another record reports a study in which an AI voice with an AI face beat every other pairing on retention, the fully human one included (Xu et al. 2025), so a human-sounding synthetic voice is not ruled out, and whether narration before a story should speak to the student at all is open in another record.

evidence.quote: **Evidence.** Personalization improves retention (*d*=0.30) and transfer (*d*=0.54) [19]. Human voice beats robotic voice at a median *d*=0.74 [20].
Direct address and a human-sounding voice create useful social cues
Monotone robotic narration in a formal textbook register.
Prefer expressive, human-like TTS and validate science pronunciation; flat robotic delivery forfeits voice and personalization benefits.
One calm, natural, grade-appropriate voice per video; conversational 2nd person ("you").
The Grade-7 default of 140–160 wpm is therefore an [OH], not a proven child threshold.
